reason: The mother is the source of the trauma, so a worried face reads as grief, not confrontation.
A boy sitting alone at homework shows isolation, not idling.
Target reads as being watched and aimed at, which is what reconnaissance means.
Respect for a general reads as status and rank; a neutral face holds the reversal.
A calculated tactician aiming at a goal, with a cold smirk, reads as scheming.
The strike rejects the reading, so the face must show denial, not neutrality.
An offered ceasefire is a hand held out against war; surprised reads as wow.
Centuries of fighting for the ceasefire is literally war.
The claim is raw rage, so the face must be angry, not worried.
An unchosen forced bond reads as being bound and controlled.
The bond that controls Teller reads as one person controlling another.
The burning thrones are the visible subject; fire shows what is burning, and the face reads as a grave judgment.
Nine hundred years of oppression reads as bound and controlled, not as a neutral chair.
Burning the thrones is the act being described, so fire shows it.
The aristocracy that funds the campaign is literally money paid for war.
A terrible tactical verdict reads as defeat with a slumped body, not a thoughtful pose.
The bond between Diem and Luther is a love bond; heart reads it literally.
An outcast shut out by the elite system reads as exclusion at a door.
A public reckoning is a legal judgment; law reads it literally.
Lumnos standing with its citizens is an intact city, which is what the beat shows.
Sweeping up ashes is the aftermath of fire, so fire names the cause.
Local leadership reads as home and community; a neutral face fits a principle.
A contract reads as a legal agreement; law is the literal reading.
Worthless titles read as indifference; trophy would read as a prize.
Half the city reduced to rubble reads as fire damage; a sad face carries the loss.
The political rule of appearance needs a face: a knowing smirk carries manipulation without an icon.
Citizens who do not care read as apathy; a blank face carries indifference.
The descended view of half mortals as abominations is contempt, shown by an angry accusing Crown.
Stepping out of hiding into the light reads as a way out; happy carries the hope of the declaration.
Inheritance reads as an estate or heir, the wrong meaning; an angry Luther rejecting blood purity shows the rejection.
